thread:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH severity - multiple runtime pods in inference-prod hit GPU OOM during prefill for model redwood-13b-v2. Link: https://rdo/incident/2419876543 :rotating_light:

maria: Oncall here. Seeing repeated OOMs and OOMKilled containers. Traffic spike on long-context route. Affected pool: gpu-large-2.

raj: I pulled logs from one of the pods — CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY while allocating KV cache during prefill. Requests are long prompts (~200k tokens) from a single customer workspace.

elaine: customer is probably doing a backfill job. Any idea on how widespread?

maria: Early numbers: ~2% of total generation traffic failing with 500s. About 3 pods restarted in last 10m.

raj: kubectl logs snippet from runtime container:
```
I0224 09:15:02.123456 1 runtime.cpp:412] prefill start, request_id=xyz
E0224 09:15:03.234567 1 cuda_driver.cpp:78] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: out of memory when allocating 45,239,040 bytes
W0224 09:15:03.234578 1 process_watcher.cpp:129] killed process 4321 (python) signal 9
I0224 09:15:03.334000 1 kubelet: Pod "runtime-abc-123" status: OOMKilled
```

maria: Thanks. I'm going to throttle the long-context route in the gateway now (rate limit to 1/s) to stop new inflight prefill requests.

ops-bot: Executing rate-limit change: gateway:set_rate_limit route=long-context limit=1/s — success.

kevin: Can we short-circuit prefill for extremely long requests (e.g., > 65k tokens)? If we can abort early we avoid large KV cache allocations.

elaine: We have PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS env but it's unset for this cluster. Suggest setting to 65536 as a temporary limit.

maria: Patching deployment to set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=65536 on runtime service. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/runtime PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=65536 -n inference-prod`

ops-bot: Rolling update triggered for deployment/runtime: 3 pods will be restarted.

raj: Also switching the customer to the quantized-13b variant (q4f16) for lower VRAM during the handoff. I'll update routing rule for that workspace.

cs-jordan: FYI CS update: Customer X reported increased 500s for their job starting ~09:12 UTC. They run background batch inference, not real-time. We told them we're mitigating and will follow up.

maria: Pod restart logs show node kernel didn't crash; it's the container process. Looks like fragmentation + big single allocation. We should still check driver version but immediate fix is in-place.

raj: Done: routing for workspace:ws-xyz -> model redwood-13b-v2-q4f16. Confirmed no more OOMs in that worker pool.

kevin: I added a soft taint on gpu-large-2 to drain noncritical jobs while we stabilize: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-large-2 spot=true:NoSchedule`

ops-bot: 3/3 runtime pods restarted successfully. Health checks pass.

maria: Running a 20m observation window. If stable, we'll lift the rate-limit gradually and monitor CPU/GPU mem.

elaine: For postmortem action items: (1) enable PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS default in deployment config, (2) add quota and warning for huge single-request token size in gateway, (3) evaluate fragmentation mitigation (cudaMallocPool or different memory allocator).

raj: Also add a fallback policy: if prefill alloc size > 32GB, route to quantized variant automatically.

cs-jordan: For customer comms: telling Customer X they've been impacted for ~25m starting 09:12 UTC, mitigation applied (throttled + moved to quantized model). They'll need a follow-up about retries/credit.

maria: Handoff to raj for overnight monitoring — he's the oncall for infra tonight. Handoff notes: throttled long-context route (1/s), set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=65536, moved heavy workspace to q4f16 variant, tainted node gpu-large-2. Pods stable as of 09:38 UTC.

raj: Acknowledged. I'll watch logs, set an alert for repeated OOMs > 1/min, and schedule driver + allocator investigation with infra tomorrow.

maria: Thanks everyone. Postmortem doc assigned to @elaine. Marking incident resolved->monitoring. :white_check_mark:
